judgements.justification: B's lone detractor Reviewer_eiQW (4) rested part of its case on wrong claims, that the DV estimator is the main computation and that no results vary the dimension; no A reviewer made these errors.
A's chair gave a spotlight at a mean of 7.0, where 32 of 44 copies got a poster, on its own reading of 'potential ... broad impact' and with no criticism weighed.
A's top score, Reviewer_imZu's 8, called the theory 'sound' with no specifics and missed the Proposition 1 error, and it lifted A's mean to 7.0 behind the spotlight.
The authors made their concessions only in answer to B's reviewers; they did not volunteer a flaw to one forum.
B weighed the conceded errors and made the DPI fix a condition; A never learned of them, and dcfo's low-dimensional point was not a substantive flaw that A knew of.
No score change is recorded in either committee after the rebuttal.
Only B found the pairwise-for-mutual error in Property 5, the dimension dependence hidden in C and M, and the misleading DPI argument; no A reviewer raised them.
Both committees saw the missing MI-estimator baselines and proof-of-concept experiments; A's dcfo called benchmarks 'probably out of scope' and rated 6 to 7, while B's eiQW gave 4 on them.
Neither chair adopted a single reviewer's position; both followed the panel.
CzLh and 6PJ4 echoed the DPI concern after reading other reviews, but neither changed a score.
The authors dismissed some of eiQW's points, but eiQW never followed up, and nothing shows a misreading held its 4 down.
A's thin reviews engaged after the rebuttal (imZu, C7hP) or made specific points (dcfo), and B's silent eiQW wrote a detailed 23-hour review.
Neither chair went below its reviewers' scores.
Both committees accepted; no chair decided acceptance by a threshold against its own view.
eiQW's 4 rested on the experiments, which are central to the paper's claims, not on a peripheral point.
Both committees read SMI as a theory-led dependence measure and judged it the same way.
C7hP, who did not check the maths, was satisfied by the rebuttal, but no score rise is recorded.
Both committees asked for the same baselines and benchmarks; they weighted them differently, which is R08, not a different requirement.
A's Reviewer_C7hP rated originality high because it read SMI as 'a new estimator of the mutual information', which the paper does not claim.
CzLh was 'satisfied' and kept 6, but 6 is above threshold, and eiQW never acknowledged the rebuttal.
Neither committee refused promised revisions; A credited the promised comparisons and B accepted with the DPI fix promised.
No reviewer's stated stance departed from its score.
No extra reviewer was called in.
Only eiQW found the writing unclear, and the other B reviewers called it well written, so expertise did not split the committees on clarity.
No reviewer raised a score silently.
B's chair called the reviews 'overwhelmingly positive' but still gave the poster its 6.0 mean set; no low rating was set aside.
Neither committee had a champion with a detailed, checked reading; A's 8 was thin.
No reviewer admitted a partial reading at high confidence.
B's DPI objection was a soundness point within the paper's own information-theoretic frame, not a rival tradition.
A's chair gave a reason for the spotlight, the measure's potential broad impact, though a thin one.
Both committees named the missing MI estimators; neither alone knew the baseline literature.
B's 'overwhelmingly positive' overstates the panel, but in the direction of a higher outcome, not the chair's lower decision.
No one in either committee objected to breadth of audience.

reasoning: The split has two parts, and existing reasons cover both. A's spotlight came from the chair's upgrade at a mean that usually gives a poster (R02), resting on a thin 8 (R03) and a reviewer who misread SMI as a new MI estimator (R19). B's lower mean came from eiQW weighting the shared experimental gap more heavily (R08), partly on wrong claims (R01), and from B's closer reading of the theory, which found three conceded errors A missed (R07). The candidate 'lone detractor' and 'closer theory reading' map to R08, R01 and R07, so no new reason is needed.
